artworks.title: Psychostasia dinos: Hermes weighing the Keres of Achilles and Memnon
artworks.description: On the rim of this Attic black-figure dinos (Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna, Antikensammlung IV 3619), found at Caere, the rare scene of the psychostasia unfolds: Hermes holds aloft a balance, and in each pan crouches a small winged figure. These winged souls are the Keres, the death-fates of Achilles and Memnon, weighed as the two heroes fight to the death between their grieving mothers Thetis and Eos. The heavier Ker tips the scale and seals its bearer's doom, dragging him down to Hades. The painter renders the abstract Hesiodic notion of fated death as a literal weighing of winged spirits, the canonical iconography by which the Keres entered Greek vase painting.

artworks.title: Psychostasia volute-krater fragments: the weighing of the souls
artworks.description: These fragments of an Attic red-figure volute-krater (Bibliotheque nationale de France, Cabinet des Medailles 385), an early work of the Kleophrades Painter found at Tarquinia, preserve another psychostasia. Zeus presides with thunderbolt and staff while Hermes, holding the kerykeion, lifts the balance to weigh the souls of two hoplites, most likely Achilles and Memnon. The Ker that sinks lower marks the warrior doomed to fall. The composition translates the moment of fate into a divine accounting, the Keres as the measurable weight of each man's death set in the gods' scales.

artworks.title: The 'Psychostasia' of Achilles and Memnon
artworks.description: The Anglo-Swiss Romantic painter Henry Fuseli revived the ancient theme of the weighing of fates in this drawing of the psychostasia of Achilles and Memnon. Reaching back past Homer to the lost Aethiopis and the vase-painters who showed Hermes balancing the heroes' death-spirits, Fuseli stages the cosmic adjudication of doom as a sublime confrontation of mothers, gods and scales. The Keres, the personified deaths weighed in the balance, here become the engine of his characteristic drama of inexorable fate.
